summary: Tokan Tada was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Akita High School and Sera Monastery (1913–1923), he held posts at the University of Tokyo (1924), Tohoku University (1925), and Toyo Bunko (1956).
Toke Lindegaard Knudsen works in Indology and history and archaeology. He studied under Kim Plofker and doctoral supervisor David Pingree (2008).

Tokio Takata is a sinologist, linguist, and Central Asian studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University and the EHESS. He held faculty posts at Otaru University of Commerce (1981–1983), Kyoto University (1983, 1997–2014), and Fudan University (2016–2022).

Tokiyoshi Hōjō studied at the University of Tokyo (~1881–1885). Over his career, he held posts at Yamaguchi University (~1894–1896), Kanazawa University (~1898–1908), and Tohoku University (~1913–1917).

Buddhist studies scholar Tokugen Sakai studied at Komazawa University, Kyoto University, and under Kodo Sawaki (1941). He served on the faculty of Komazawa University (1949–1987) and taught at Eihei-ji (1977–1987).

Tokuno Oda was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Fukui Prefectural Normal School, Otani University, and under Gaju Ikehara and Junjirō Takakusu. He held teaching posts at Fukui Prefectural Normal School, Fukui Prefectural Fujishima High School, and Toyo University.

Philosopher Tokuryu Yamauchi studied at Kyoto University, the University of Freiburg, and under Kitaro Nishida and Martin Heidegger. His career included professorships at Hitotsubashi University, Kyoto University, Ryukoku University, and the presidency of Kyoto University of Education.
Tom De Rauw is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies who completed his doctoral studies under Ann Heirman. He held an AAP post at Ghent University (attested 2026).

Tom Ginsburg, a scholar of law and Buddhist studies, studied at the University of California, Berkeley (~1985–1999). He held a post at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (~2000–2008) before joining the University of Chicago (~2008).

Tom Tillemans is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy who studied under Jacques May. He served as Emeritus Professor of Buddhist Studies at the University of Lausanne (attested 1987–2018) and held the Visiting Numata Chair at the University of Calgary.
Tomohiro Manabe specializes in Indology and philosophy. He has held academic posts at Waseda University (attested 2020) and Hokkaido University as an associate professor (attested 2026).

Tomoko Makidono works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. She held a researcher post at Minobusan University (attested 2015) and was a doctoral student at the University of Hamburg (attested 2026).

Tomoko Masuzawa works in religious studies and history/archaeology. She studied at International Christian University, Yale, and UC Santa Barbara, and held academic posts at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill (~1987–2001) and the University of Michigan (from 1999).
Tomomichi Nitta is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He held a lecturer post at Otani University (attested 2012) and a professorship at the Otani Academic Society (attested 2026).
Tomoyasu Oshima is an Indologist who studied under Toshifumi Goto and held a part-time lecturer post at Kyoto University (attested 2012).
Tomoyuki Komine is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University, where he also served as a part-time lecturer (attested 2015).

Tomoyuki Uno works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He served as a special researcher for the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (attested 1998) and as an assistant professor at Chikushi Jogakuen University (attested 2000–2006).

Tomy Augustine is a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He earned degrees from the University of Madras and Banaras Hindu University, studying under C. S. Sundaram and Munni K. Agrawal, and held a post at Salesian College (attested 2008).

Toni Huber specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Canterbury under Paul Harrison and William S. Sax, and held professorships at Victoria University of Wellington (attested 2000) and Humboldt University of Berlin (attested 2006–2008).

Tony K. Stewart is an Indology and religious studies scholar educated at Western Kentucky University (~1972–1976). He held posts at North Carolina State University (~1986–2011) and Vanderbilt University (~2011).
